gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold bundles two distinct failures: applying a full-space rank-one uniqueness theorem to the row-space completion construction, and relying on the wrong global rank-one uniqueness/rank condition. ISSUE-013 independently diagnoses the fixed-factor fiber versus global matching distinction and supplies the complementary-span repair; ISSUE-012 independently diagnoses the absent rank-one uniqueness hypothesis and its failure. Together they cover the full concern.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The completion argument must use the actual complementary-factor row space and a uniqueness condition appropriate to the fixed known-factor fiber, rather than treating the differently parameterized full matching space and its unrestricted rank-one uniqueness condition as interchangeable. No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised; the predictions demonstrate the two components through a fixed-factor example and a counterexample to unrestricted uniqueness.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: The predictions use different examples and phrase the space mismatch through fixed-factor fibers and complementary spans rather than explicitly contrasting every displayed theorem notation; no substantive gold concern is left unrecognised.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold entry contains independently diagnosable components: (1) the cited theorem concerns the wrong matching object for the algorithm's row-space completion step, diagnosed by ISSUE-013's fixed-factor/complementary-span analysis; and (2) the uniqueness/rank-one-point condition needed for the matching step is not an unrestricted consequence of the stated hypotheses, diagnosed self-containedly by ISSUE-012's counterexample and repair. Both entries are necessary and each independently supports its assigned component.
